title: Buck Converter (step-down)
summary: Non-isolated step-down converter; in continuous conduction the output voltage equals the input scaled by the duty cycle D.

ports.name: sw
ports.description: Switching node between the high-side switch, the freewheeling diode/synchronous switch, and the inductor.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Regulated step-down output rail across the filter capacitor and load.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive command for the high-side switch from the controller.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of the high-side switch.

parameters.name: R_load
parameters.description: Load resistance seen at the output (R_load = Vout / Iout).

parameters.name: r_L
parameters.description: Inductor series resistance (DCR); dominant loss term affecting the DC conversion ratio.

parameters.name: r_C
parameters.description: Output capacitor equivalent series resistance (ESR); sets the high-frequency zero.

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio_with_losses
design_equations.description: CCM DC conversion ratio including the inductor series resistance r_L (Alonso eq. 1.6); the capacitor ESR does not affect the DC ratio because no DC current flows in C.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average inductor current equals the load current in CCM.

design_equations.name: inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak inductor current ripple in CCM.

design_equations.name: peak_device_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through the switch, diode, and inductor in CCM.

design_equations.name: switch_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak blocking voltage across the switch (and the diode) is the input voltage.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in CCM for an ideal capacitor (ESR adds r_C * dI_L on top).

design_equations.name: critical_inductance
design_equations.description: Minimum inductance to stay in continuous conduction at the given load.

design_equations.name: boundary_load_resistance
design_equations.description: CCM-DCM boundary load resistance (Alonso eq. 1.29): CCM when R_load < R_lim, DCM when R_load > R_lim.

design_equations.name: boundary_output_current
design_equations.description: Output current at the CCM-DCM boundary (Alonso eq. 1.28).

design_equations.name: dcm_conversion_ratio
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = 2 / (1 + sqrt(1 + 4 * k / D**2)),  k = 2 * L * fsw / R_load
design_equations.description: DCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 1.40-1.41); it is load-dependent and r_L drops out because the converter acts as a current source into the load.

design_equations.name: dcm_output_ripple
design_equations.expression: dVout = L / (2 * C * (1 - Vout / Vin) * Vout) * ((Vin - Vout) * D / (L * fsw) - Vout / R_load)**2
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in DCM (Alonso eq. 1.46).

design_equations.name: ccm_characteristic_polynomial
design_equations.expression: Den(s) = L*C*(1 + r_C/R_load)*s**2 + (L/R_load + r_C*C + r_L*C + r_L*r_C*C/R_load)*s + (1 + r_L/R_load)
design_equations.description: Shared CCM denominator (characteristic polynomial) of every small-signal transfer function below; a complex pole pair near 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C)).

design_equations.name: control_to_output_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Control-to-output (duty-cycle to output) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 1.14); single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C), no right-half-plane zero.

design_equations.name: audio_susceptibility_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Input-to-output (audio susceptibility) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 1.17); same dynamics as Gd(s), only the DC gain differs.

design_equations.name: output_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop output impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 1.23); Zo(0) approx r_L, Zo(inf) approx r_C.

design_equations.name: input_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop input impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 1.19); the characteristic polynomial appears in the numerator, with Zi(0) = (R_load + r_L)/D**2 and Zi(inf) -> infinity.

control_notes: The buck control-to-output plant Gd(s) is a second-order low-pass with a complex pole pair at the LC resonance and a single ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C); it has no right-half-plane zero, so voltage-mode control with a Type-II/Type-III compensator is straightforward. Cross over well below fsw/5. Peak/average current-mode control reduces the plant to first order and eases loop design. In discontinuous conduction (DCM, when R_load > R_lim = 2*L*fsw/(1-D)) the plant also collapses to a first-order response and the DC gain becomes load-dependent. All small-signal results follow from the averaged dependent-source model: the switch is replaced by its average current source and the diode by its average voltage source, then linearized about the DC operating point.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
